text:
kevin: Quick sync: our golden input set is drifting. New models pass local golden but fail in prod subsets. Thoughts on maintenance cadence?

tanya: We should derive a rolling golden from real traffic weekly, not static canned files. Keep a stable canonical for audits but use a shadow-derived set for perf checks.

sasha: Watch out for PII in traffic-derived sets. Need an automated sanitizer + heuristic to drop sensitive queries. Also strip long user IDs.

aj: Can we augment traffic samples with adversarial perturbations? e.g., tokenization edgecases, long-tail punctuation, unicode. Cheap synthetic boosts coverage without full retrain corpora.

ramon: Operationally: two-tier golden plan. 1) canonical-release-set (stable, human-reviewed) 2) rolling-shadow-set (1 week sliding window, auto-sanitized). Admission gate runs rolling-shadow-sweep; deep-eval uses canonical.

elaine: For the rolling set, include metadata per sample: source-hash, anonymization-level, average-seqlen, kv-hit-prob. That helps debug when a sample triggers a regression.

bench-bot: sample-collector: last-week 12.4M requests, sampled 8k candidates -> sanitized 2.1k -> final rolling 500. Top buckets: short-chitchat 42%, completion-long 21%, code 8%.

mina: Nice. A few open tradeoffs: frequency (weekly vs nightly), cost (500 deep runs scales), and reproducibility (we must be able to rehydrate a rolling set for audits). Proposal: nightly lightweight probes on 100 rolling samples, weekly deep sweep on 500.

kevin: Makes sense. How to pick which 500 for weekly deep? Random stratified by traffic buckets + golden-suspect heuristics (tokenizer changes, new special tokens).

aj: Also add a mutation pass when tokenizer or vocab changes: take N traffic samples, run small perturbation matrix (replace punctuation, strip spaces, utf8 noise) and include any that flip model outputs. These are high-signal for regressions.

ramon: About gating: treat output-quality flips separately from perf regressions. If a sample changes classification/stop-criteria, mark for human review. We shouldn't auto-fail on subtle text diffs.

elaine: Agree. Bench report schema needs fields: sample_id, sample_bucket, seqlen, kv_warm_flag, tokenizer_fingerprint, model_fingerprint, output_hash, diff_reason. Put that in ingest payload.

bench-bot: action: created ticket ML-boarding-512: rolling-golden-pipeline + sanitizer + schema.

mina: Action items: ramon to prototype sanitizer + rehydration tool, tanya to define sampling policy + stratification weights, aj to spec mutation matrix, elaine to draft report schema, kevin + mina to write gating playbook for diff thresholds and human-review flow. I'll collect in a short RFC and tag reviewers. :thumbsup:
